In 1922, Woodcraft Rangers opened its doors in Los Angeles and began its mission of guiding young people as they explore pathways to purposeful lives. Any person occupying a position under exempt appointment shall not be subject to civil service selection, appointment, and removal procedures. Exempt appointees are considered "at will" and shall serve at the discretion of the Appointing Officer.

**About the Port of San Francisco**


The Port of San Francisco is steward to one of the world’s most iconic waterfronts – a dynamic 7\.5\-mile stretch along the San Francisco Bay. With a diverse real estate portfolio, active maritime operations, and hundreds of tenants including Pier 39, the Ferry Building, Oracle Park, and the Exploratorium, the Port plays a central role in the city’s economic vitality, cultural identity, and global reputation. Our dedicated employees operate marinas and piers, maintain historic public spaces, and partner with the private sector to revitalize neighborhoods and deliver transformative development and open space projects.


Over the past decade, the Port has evolved into a strategically driven agency known for innovation, equity, and impact. Through bold initiatives in economic recovery, resilience, and public\-private partnerships, the Port has secured historic investments and created a strong foundation for the waterfront’s next chapter. With over $13\.5 billion in planned resilience infrastructure and more than 60 acres of new waterfront neighborhoods under development, the Port is leading the way in adapting San Francisco’s shoreline for future generations.


The Port’s mission is grounded in stewardship, partnership, and public service. We are building a workplace rooted in inclusion and belonging and shaping a waterfront where all are welcome. We invite you to join a team that is not only transforming the city’s shoreline but also setting a new standard for public sector excellence and innovation.

The Executive Director will retain direct management for the Executive and Finance and Administration divisions. The Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer will be charged with overseeing the work program for the operating divisions: Real Estate and Development; Maritime; Maintenance; Engineering; and Planning and Environment. The Deputy Directors for each of these divisions will be direct reports to the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer. Because the Waterfront Resilience Program is at a key strategic point in its development as it pivots from conceptual planning to design of specific segments of the line of defense, the Executive Director and the Assistant Port Director will share management of this division for a period of time before it eventually transitions to the Assistant Port Director’s operating portfolio.


For more information on each of these divisions, please see our website at: https://www.sfport.com/about/divisions\-and\-staff

**The Executive Division**


The second key function for the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer is to contribute to the development and management of strategic direction for the full organization as a member of the Executive Division. The team is also charged with ensuring public safety along the waterfront including during major civic events.

**Position Title:** SUD Program Director

**SCHEDULE:** Full\-time position. Onsite/Hybrid


**BENEFITS:** Health, Dental, and Vision insurance; Commuter stipend

 **About Homeless Children’s Network (HCN)**



Since 1992, HCN has been San Francisco’s leading nonprofit agency for comprehensive early intervention and mental health support for underserved and historically marginalized children, youth, and families experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or living in intergenerational poverty. Our mobile therapeutic model is both accessible and scalable, enabling clinicians to meet clients directly in the community. As the hub of a Collaborative of 60\+ service agencies and community\-based organizations, we serve over 2,500 clients each year, reaching those most reluctant to trust conventional mental health systems. Central to our work is our Afri\-centric mental health and wellness model. This community\-defined approach addresses health inequities and the persistent cycle of racism and trauma over generations. This model not only uplifts the Black/African American communities but also strengthens the behavioral health outcomes of all San Franciscans, fostering resilience, healing, and lasting change.

 **KUPONA SUD OUTPATIENT PROGRAM OVERVIEW:**

  

Kupona Program is a culturally responsive and family\-centered substance use treatment program for youth in San Francisco. Utilizing Evidence\-based and locally\-innovative interventions, this program will provide co\-occurring or SUD standalone services for youth who are at risk or struggling with drug, alcohol, and other substances. Kupona offers a continuum of services depending on the level of care needed:


* Early Intervention for youth who are at risk of developing a Substance Use Disorder (SUD),
* Outpatient Level 1 for youth who are actively using substances and meet criteria for SUD diagnosis, but who present with NO acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential.
* Intensive Outpatient for youth who are actively using substances, meet criteria for SUD diagnosis, and who present with acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential.
* This program serves all ethnicities and populations within San Francisco with focused expertise to meet the needs of youth under the age of 18 years old who are Medi\-Cal beneficiaries.

  


**POSITION SUMMARY:**



The SUD Program Director is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day operations of HCN’s youth substance use disorder (SUD) treatment program, including clinical services, staff management, client care, compliance with regulations, and ensuring the delivery of high\-quality and evidence\-based treatment under the Drug Medi\-Cal (DMC\-ODS) framework. The School of Humanities and Sciences (H\&S) is Stanford's largest school, with 24 top\-ranked academic departments and dozens of programs, centers, and institutes spanning the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. H\&S teaches the majority of undergraduates in its majors, trains roughly 40% of Stanford PhDs, and produces knowledge that adds to humanity’s inheritance. The school sits at the intellectual core of the university, and its faculty and students drive discovery across expansive fields of inquiry.


The H\&S Development team partners with the Dean's office, department chairs, center directors, and colleagues across University Development to secure philanthropic support for the school's most pressing priorities — from named professorships and graduate fellowships to research initiatives and capital projects. As H\&S works toward an ambitious fundraising goal amid a competitive philanthropic landscape, the team is focused on building a robust pipeline of new donors and deepening relationships with existing supporters.

The H\&S development team is seeking candidates for an Associate Director of Development, reporting to the Director of Development. This is an excellent opportunity for a fundraiser who enjoys the front end of the philanthropic process — building relationships, uncovering giving capacity and interest, and helping shape a donor's philanthropic journey from the very first conversation.


This role will work from a robust pool of qualified prospects to build and manage a discovery\-focused major gift portfolio across a range of academic clusters within H\&S. jobs.title: Executive Director, Stanford University Metabolic Center (Hybrid Opportunity)
jobs.description:
The Stanford University School of Medicine ( Department of Medicine ) is launching the Stanford University Metabolic Center , a premier initiative uniting department across the School of Medicine and Stanford Health Care around one of the most consequential health challenges of our time: the epidemic of metabolic disease. We are seeking the Center's inaugural Executive Director to help build and lead this center from the ground up.


This is a ground\-floor opportunity. As the first Executive Director, you won't inherit a center; you will help create one: by building its research infrastructure, forging the clinical\-academic partnerships that will define how it operates for years to come, and establishing the philanthropic and industry relationships that will fuel its growth. Few roles in academic medicine offer this level of scope, visibility, and latitude to shape an institution's future.


The Center’s vision is to close the gap between discovery and care, connecting four research cores (Basic Science, Translational \& Data Science, Precision Population Health, and Clinical Trials) directly to a Hub \& Spoke clinical model across Stanford Health Care, so that advances in metabolic science move seamlessly from bench to bedside. Guided by Executive Sponsors, Dr. Euan Ashley and Dr. Fatima Rodriguez, and led by Faculty Director, Dr. Paul Kwo, and Associate Faculty Director, Dr. Sun Kim, the Center is built on the premise that the next era of metabolic medicine will be won by institutions that can integrate research, clinical care, education, and philanthropy into a single, coordinated engine and the Executive Director is who makes that integration real.


Reporting to this leadership team, the Executive Director will lead, manage, and administer the Center’s strategic, academic, research, and educational operations with minimal supervision. You will drive the Center's university\-side vision, build robust philanthropic and industry pipelines, oversee its research cores, and direct multidisciplinary educational programs, while partnering closely with Stanford Health Care’s Clinical Operations Directors to keep research and clinical care in lockstep.


This is a hybrid role and will require an on\-site presence 3 days per week from our Redwood City Offices or the School of Medicine Campus in Palo Alto, with the option to work the remaining 2 days from a non\-Stanford site, such as home.  



**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* **Integrate research and clinical care.** Lead the operational integration of the Center's four Research Cores with Stanford Health Care's clinical pathways, ensuring patient intake flows seamlessly into recruitment registries and biobanking, and aligning the Hub \& Spoke clinic model with active research protocols and data pipelines.
* **Drive School of Medicine alignment.** Build strategic alignment and collaboration across research programs, departments, and divisions throughout the School of Medicine, coordinating their work within the Center's four core areas.
* **Build the Center’s infrastructure.** Partner with the Research Manager to plan equipment and lab infrastructure from freezers to secure biospecimen storage that will support the Center's research for years to come.
* **Shape the Center’s direction.** Evaluate programs, policies, and operational trends from biobank throughput to philanthropic and NIH/NIDDK funding cycles and advise Center leadership on strategy, resourcing, and growth.
* **Represent the Center.** Serve as the School of Medicine's primary administrative representative for the Center, liaising across Medicine, Pediatrics, Genetics, Biomedical Data Science, and Engineering, and present regularly to the Center's Executive Sponsors and Board.
* **Launch new ventures.** Stand up the Industry Affiliates Program, establishing corporate sponsorships and biotechnology partnerships that will help fund the Center's research mission.
* **Own the budget and philanthropy pipeline.** Design and manage the Center’s operational budget, including endowment funding, multi\-year philanthropy, and industry revenue, in partnership with the Medical School's Development team.
* **Build the team.** Supervise research and administrative staff and support the Center’s physician education and CME programs for the next generation of metabolic disease clinicians.

If you’re energized by the idea of building something new or being the operational architect behind a center that will shape how Stanford and the field approach metabolic disease, we encourage you to apply.


  
**Core Duties** :


* Lead strategic planning and analysis for complex functions or programs with significant business, regulatory and/or technical challenges requiring subject matter expertise. May provide development of program or function from initial concept to implementation.
* Manage the administration and evaluation of programs or functions. Oversee the interpretation, implementation and compliance with policies and regulations. Recommend actions and/or resolve complex issues that often span organizational boundaries.

Hope House is seeking an inspiring and mission\-driven leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer.

For more than three decades, Hope House has been a trusted leader in addressing homelessness and housing instability in Northwest Ohio. Through shelter services, supportive programming, advocacy, and community partnerships, Hope House helps individuals and families move toward stability and self\-sufficiency.

**About the Port of San Francisco**


The Port of San Francisco is steward to one of the world’s most iconic waterfronts – a dynamic 7\.5\-mile stretch along the San Francisco Bay. With a diverse real estate portfolio, active maritime operations, and hundreds of tenants including Pier 39, the Ferry Building, Oracle Park, and the Exploratorium, the Port plays a central role in the city’s economic vitality, cultural identity, and global reputation. Our dedicated employees operate marinas and piers, maintain historic public spaces, and partner with the private sector to revitalize neighborhoods and deliver transformative development and open space projects.


Over the past decade, the Port has evolved into a strategically driven agency known for innovation, equity, and impact. Through bold initiatives in economic recovery, resilience, and public\-private partnerships, the Port has secured historic investments and created a strong foundation for the waterfront’s next chapter. With over $13\.5 billion in planned resilience infrastructure and more than 60 acres of new waterfront neighborhoods under development, the Port is leading the way in adapting San Francisco’s shoreline for future generations.


The Port’s mission is grounded in stewardship, partnership, and public service. We are building a workplace rooted in inclusion and belonging and shaping a waterfront where all are welcome. We invite you to join a team that is not only transforming the city’s shoreline but also setting a new standard for public sector excellence and innovation.


For more information about the Port of San Francisco, visit SFPort.com. Follow us on Twitter and Facebook.

**Port Organizational Structure**


The Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer will have two key functions of equal importance. The first of these is to provide day\-to\-day management and tactical oversight for the Port’s operating divisions.


The Port of San Francisco is comprised of eight divisions: Executive; Finance and Administration; Real Estate and Development; Maritime; Maintenance; Engineering; Planning and Environment; and the Waterfront Resilience Program. The Executive Director will retain direct management for the Executive and Finance and Administration divisions. The Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer will be charged with overseeing the work program for the operating divisions: Real Estate and Development; Maritime; Maintenance; Engineering; and Planning and Environment. The Deputy Directors for each of these divisions will be direct reports to the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer. Because the Waterfront Resilience Program is at a key strategic point in its development as it pivots from conceptual planning to design of specific segments of the line of defense, the Executive Director and the Assistant Port Director will share management of this division for a period of time before it eventually transitions to the Assistant Port Director’s operating portfolio.


For more information on each of these divisions, please see our website at: https://www.sfport.com/about/divisions\-and\-staff

**The Executive Division**


The second key function for the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer is to contribute to the development and management of strategic direction for the full organization as a member of the Executive Division. The Executive Division reports directly to the Port Executive Director and includes the Assistant Port Director/Chief Operating Officer, Communications, Government Affairs, Equity, Inclusion \& Diversity, Security, Port Commission Secretary and the Port's General Counsel.

* **Communications, Government Affairs** and **Equity, Inclusion and Diversity** develop and execute strategic initiatives in each applicable area.
